advances: Fixed body and positive affine multiplier optimization. The larger singleton has weight $3/2>M/2=5/4$ and violates its proper-minor quota. Its ordinary raw maximum $3/4$ exceeds the sharp $n=d=1$ target $M/4=5/8$.

proof:
The sampled intervals are exactly the sections at $0,1$. The only integer bases are those two sites. Their centered second moments are $a^3/12,b^3/12$, so $\Sigma=(a^3+b^3)/(12M)=7/48$. The accepted interval projective-energy formula in efa4558174ce60cf uses the distances $V/2+y$ and $V/2-y$ from $y$ to the two endpoints. It gives $E_V(y)=V-4y^2/V$ in the interior and the stated continuous zero extension. The geometric mean weights are $a/M=2/5$ and $b/M=3/5$, giving $\ell_a^2\ell_b^3=1$. Every positive pair gives an affine function positive on $[0,1]$.

For a nonvertical through-mark cap, divide its normal by the absolute value of its continuous coefficient. The own trace then has sign $+1$ or $-1$ in the continuous coordinate, and its buffered mass is the corresponding endpoint-to-threshold length clipped at $V$. The better of these masses is $\min(V,V/2-|y|+\delta_i(y))$. No other fiber lowers it. For either sign a sufficiently large finite base tilt directed toward the chosen endpoint excludes the other interval and preserves that own trace. A pure-base containing cap captures at least $V$ and a pure-base isolating cap attains $V$. Allowing any initially containing rather than through-mark halfspace cannot improve the infimum, since translating its boundary to the mark before applying the fixed mark buffer only decreases its trace. This proves the exact all-normal depth formula. As $|y|$ increases, the unsaturated expression strictly decreases because of the term $-|y|$ and the nonincreasing energy. This gives the fiber maximum and its stated uniqueness.

Write $e=\varepsilon c$ and $t=\ell_a$. The two midpoint shifts are $e\sqrt t$ and $e\sqrt{3/2}\,t^{-1/3}$. Their fourth and sixth powers have product $(3/2)^3e^{10}$. The two unsaturated fiber maximum formulas strictly increase and strictly decrease, respectively, with $t$. For $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_*$ the displayed equation has exactly one root in $(3/4,1)$, since its left side increases from $0$ to $1/65536$. The stated multipliers at this root give the two midpoint shifts, satisfy the product constraint, and meet below either saturation level. A smaller or larger $t$ strictly increases one of the two fiber maxima, because even the saturated value of that branch is greater than $q_\varepsilon$. This proves uniqueness, the list of buffered maximizers, and the properness of the two own cuts. The root tends to $3/4$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ by the same monotonicity. Hence $\varepsilon^2\ell_a\to(1/4)^2/c^2=15/14$, the other multiplier follows from $\ell_b=\ell_a^{-2/3}$, and the shifts follow from $q_\varepsilon-1/2$ and $q_\varepsilon-3/4$. At zero buffer the two unshifted midpoint values are $1/2$ and $3/4$, respectively.

At and above $\varepsilon_*$ a maximum below $1$ would require both midpoint shifts to be strictly below $1/2$ and $1/4$, which violates the product constraint. Setting the larger fiber's shift to $1/4$ realizes optimal value $1$ and gives the specified smaller shift. In fact every larger $t$ also gives value $1$, since the smaller fiber is already saturated and the larger branch is decreasing. At the threshold only the parameter where both formulas meet has both midpoint shifts equal to the stated values. The two smaller-fiber continuous orientations capture all of its own interval at that parameter or the specified higher-$\varepsilon$ multipliers. Use the finite isolating tilt to attain the minimizing ambient cap with that trace.

statement:
Let $C$ be the trapezoid obtained as the convex hull of centered intervals of lengths $a=1$ and $b=3/2$ at the consecutive bases $0$ and $1$. Use mixed length $M=5/2$, pooled within-fiber variance $\Sigma=7/48$ and $c^2=\Sigma/M=7/120$. For a centered interval of length $V$ use projective energy $E_V(y)=V-4y^2/V$ on $[-V/2,V/2]$, extended by zero at the endpoints. Impose positive affine multipliers with $\ell_a^2\ell_b^3=1$. At the mark $(i,y)$ in the interval of length $V$, move the threshold of every through-mark cap with continuous coefficient of unit magnitude outward by $\delta_i(y)=\varepsilon c\sqrt{\ell_i E_V(y)}$, leaving pure-base caps unchanged. The exact buffered raw depth is $\min\{V,V/2-|y|+\delta_i(y)\}$, and the fiber maximum is $\min\{V,V/2+\varepsilon c\sqrt{\ell_i V}\}$, achieved at the midpoint and uniquely so when the latter value is below $V$.

Define $\varepsilon_*^{10}=120^5/(221184\cdot7^5)$. For $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_*$ the buffered maximum over both fibers has a unique minimizing multiplier. Its optimal value $q_\varepsilon$ is the unique root in $(3/4,1)$ of
$$
(q-1/2)^4(q-3/4)^6=(3/2)^3(\varepsilon c)^{10}.
$$
At the minimizing multiplier,
$$
\ell_a=\frac{(q_\varepsilon-1/2)^2}{\varepsilon^2c^2},
\qquad
\ell_b=\frac{(q_\varepsilon-3/4)^2}{(3/2)\varepsilon^2c^2}.
$$
The only buffered maximizing marks are the two midpoints and their minimizing nonvertical own cuts are proper. As $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, $q_\varepsilon\to3/4$, $\varepsilon^2\ell_a\to15/14$, $\ell_b\sim(14/15)^{2/3}\varepsilon^{4/3}$, and the midpoint shifts tend to $1/4$ and $0$, respectively. The ordinary maximum is $3/4$, attained only at the larger midpoint.

At $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_*$ the optimal value is $1$ and the two unsaturated formulas meet at shifts $1/2$ and $1/4$. For every $\varepsilon>\varepsilon_*$ the optimal value is again $1$, with an optimizer whose shifts are strictly greater than $1/2$ and equal to $1/4$, respectively. At these specified optimizing multipliers for $\varepsilon\ge\varepsilon_*$ a minimizing nonvertical cap captures the whole smaller interval, as does a pure-base isolating cap. The smaller own trace is supporting at the specified crossing multiplier for $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_*$.
title: An attained affine buffer optimum with a nonvanishing shift
